subject: sentences
title: Spring sentences
about: Fifteen sentences using the spellings CKLA Units 5 to 7 add in spring: tch, soft g and c (ge, ce, se), ve, wr, kn, wh, n as in pink, and ai, ay, oa, plus the tricky words how, picture, cow and talk. By May he should read these smoothly with expression.
tip: Read one sentence each, taking turns, and let him catch you if you read too flat.

cards.text: The dog can catch the stick.
cards.note: tch says /ch/ in catch; ck in stick says /k/

cards.text: We had a huge slice of cake.
cards.note: ge in huge: g says /j/; ce in slice: c says /s/; a_e in cake says long a

cards.text: The prince has a white horse.
cards.note: ce in prince says /s/; wh in white says /w/; se in horse says /s/
wr in write says /r/; i_e in write says long i

cards.text: I bumped my knee on the bed.
cards.note: kn in knee says /n/; ee says long e; bumped: ed says /t/

cards.text: The train waits in the rain.
cards.note: ai says long a in train, waits and rain

cards.text: We can play all day in May.
cards.note: ay says long a in play, day and May; May is a month, capital M; all is a tricky word
oa says long o in goat and oats; a_e in ate says long a

cards.text: How did the cow get on the boat?
cards.note: how and cow are tricky words: ow says /ow/; oa in boat says long o; a question goes up at the end
wh says /w/ in which and whale; biggest has two parts: big + gest; a question goes up at the end

cards.text: Let's talk and look at the picture.
cards.note: talk is a tricky word: al says /aw/; picture is a tricky word; Let's is short for let us

cards.text: The pink fence is wet with paint.
cards.note: n in pink says /ng/; ce in fence says /s/; ai in paint says long a

cards.text: The mice have a big cage.
cards.note: ce in mice: c says /s/; ge in cage: g says /j/; have is a tricky word

cards.text: Grace gave twelve seeds to the hen.
cards.note: Grace is a name, capital G, and ce says /s/; ve in gave and twelve says /v/; ee in seeds says long e
ay in stay says long a; th in path; Jake is a name, capital J; the ! means read it with feeling
